headlines.title: King tides, powerful waves and incoming storm threaten Northern California coast
headlines.description: What to Know Coastal flood warning in effect until 4 p.m. Thursday. Flood warning in Solano County expires at 4 p.m. Thursday. Dense fog advisory set to expire 11 a.m. Monday in parts of the North Bay. High surf warning starts midnight Tuesday to midnight Wednesday night. Coastal flood advisory in effect until 4 p.m. Thursday. The highest tides are expected Wednesday morning. At the San Francisco tide gauge, water levels could reach 8.5 feet, or 2.7 feet above normal, at 10:49 a.m. Coastal flooding, heavy rain, strong winds and dangerous surf are expected to affect the Bay Area through Thanksgiving week, with the strongest storm impacts projected for Tuesday into Wednesday morning, according to the National Weather Service. Here’s a look at what to expect and the latest weather alerts: Coastal flood warning in effect through Thursday Major to extreme coastal flooding is possible in some areas, while a storm could bring moderate to heavy rain and wind gusts of up to 40 mph. Conditions are expected to improve for Thanksgiving Day and Friday before rain returns over the weekend. A coastal flood warning is in effect for bayshore locations along San Francisco and San Pablo bays through 4 p.m. Thursday. A Coastal Flood Advisory covers California’s Pacific Coast through the same time, the NWS says. High tides could flood low-lying roads and infrastructure, cause road closures and increase coastal erosion. The highest tides are expected Wednesday morning. At the San Francisco tide gauge, water levels could reach 8.5 feet, or 2.7 feet above normal, at 10:49 a.m. Flooding Nov 22 El Niño Oct 20 El Niño Sep 21 High surf warning with breaking waves expected to reach 20 to 30 feet The coast is also expected to face dangerous surf Wednesday, with breaking waves reaching 20 to 30 feet. A high surf warning is forecast, followed by hazardous beach conditions through the weekend. High tides could push waves farther up beaches, leaving beachgoers with less room to escape, according to the NWS. Expect more flooding in the next round of rain starting Tuesday Rain is expected Tuesday into Wednesday morning, with flooding possible in creeks, small streams, urban areas and locations with poor drainage. Some areas also face a chance of thunderstorms. Wind gusts projected to hit 30 to 40 mph across Bay Area Wind gusts of 30 to 40 mph are expected across much of the region Tuesday into Wednesday morning. Strong winds could blow around unsecured objects, break tree limbs and cause power outages. Wet ground could increase the risk of trees falling, forecasters warn. Will it rain on Thanksgiving Day and Black Friday? The weather is expected to dry out for Thanksgiving Day and Friday, offering a brief break from the storm. Rain is predicted to return Saturday into Sunday, accompanied by gusty winds and continued coastal hazards. Residents in flood-prone areas are urged to protect their property and prepare for possible road closures. Drivers should never go around barricades or drive through water of unknown depth. Beachgoers are urged to stay away from dangerous surf, beaches, jetties and rocks, where large waves can sweep people into the ocean, according to the weather service.

Dense fog advisory set to expire 11 a.m. Monday in parts of the North Bay. High surf warning starts midnight Tuesday to midnight Wednesday night. Coastal flood advisory in effect until 4 p.m. Thursday. The highest tides are expected Wednesday morning. At the San Francisco tide gauge, water levels could reach 8.5 feet, or 2.7 feet above normal, at 10:49 a.m. Coastal flooding, heavy rain, strong winds and dangerous surf are expected to affect the Bay Area through Thanksgiving week, with the strongest storm impacts projected for Tuesday into Wednesday morning, according to the National Weather Service. Here’s a look at what to expect and the latest weather alerts: Coastal flood warning in effect through Thursday Major to extreme coastal flooding is possible in some areas, while a storm could bring moderate to heavy rain and wind gusts of up to 40 mph. Conditions are expected to improve for Thanksgiving Day and Friday before rain returns over the weekend. A coastal flood warning is in effect for bayshore locations along San Francisco and San Pablo bays through 4 p.m. Thursday. A Coastal Flood Advisory covers California’s Pacific Coast through the same time, the NWS says. High tides could flood low-lying roads and infrastructure, cause road closures and increase coastal erosion. The highest tides are expected Wednesday morning. At the San Francisco tide gauge, water levels could reach 8.5 feet, or 2.7 feet above normal, at 10:49 a.m. Flooding Nov 22 El Niño Oct 20 El Niño Sep 21 High surf warning with breaking waves expected to reach 20 to 30 feet The coast is also expected to face dangerous surf Wednesday, with breaking waves reaching 20 to 30 feet. A high surf warning is forecast, followed by hazardous beach conditions through the weekend. High tides could push waves farther up beaches, leaving beachgoers with less room to escape, according to the NWS. Expect more flooding in the next round of rain starting Tuesday Rain is expected Tuesday into Wednesday morning, with flooding possible in creeks, small streams, urban areas and locations with poor drainage. Some areas also face a chance of thunderstorms. Wind gusts projected to hit 30 to 40 mph across Bay Area Wind gusts of 30 to 40 mph are expected across much of the region Tuesday into Wednesday morning. Strong winds could blow around unsecured objects, break tree limbs and cause power outages. Wet ground could increase the risk of trees falling, forecasters warn. Will it rain on Thanksgiving Day and Black Friday? The weather is expected to dry out for Thanksgiving Day and Friday, offering a brief break from the storm. Rain is predicted to return Saturday into Sunday, accompanied by gusty winds and continued coastal hazards. Residents in flood-prone areas are urged to protect their property and prepare for possible road closures. Drivers should never go around barricades or drive through water of unknown depth. Beachgoers are urged to stay away from dangerous surf, beaches, jetties and rocks, where large waves can sweep people into the ocean, according to the weather service.
